text: Ever wondered why oxygen slips straight through the membrane around a cell, while a sodium ion, tiny as it is, gets turned back unless a protein lets it through? Think about everything that membrane has to manage. It has to keep the cell's contents in, yet let the right substances across. It has to stay in one piece, yet stay flexible. And it carries the molecules that let a cell receive signals and be recognised by other cells. One thin membrane does all of that, because different molecules in it do different jobs.
